instruction: Cook the dry rice in water according to its package. Slice the beef thinly; cut the broccoli and pak choi into bite-sized pieces and mince the garlic and ginger.
Mix the shoyu, oyster sauce and cornstarch with 40 ml water per serving until smooth.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Stir-fry the beef for 3-5 minutes until cooked through, then transfer it to a plate.
Stir-fry the garlic, ginger, broccoli and pak choi for 3 minutes. Add a splash of water, cover and steam for 2-3 minutes until the vegetables are tender-crisp.
Return the beef, add the sauce and stir for 1-2 minutes until thickened and hot throughout. Serve over the rice.
Slice the tomato and onion and wash the lettuce. Divide the minced beef into one patty per burger bun and season with the salt and black pepper.
Cook the bacon in a frying pan until crisp, then remove it. Cook the patties in the same pan over medium-high heat for about 4-5 minutes per side, until the centre reaches 71 C.
Add the cheddar to the patties during the final minute and cover briefly to melt. Toast the cut sides of the buns in the pan.
Spread the mayonnaise on the buns. Assemble with lettuce, tomato, onion, patties and bacon, and serve immediately.
Cook the dry spaghetti in water seasoned with the listed salt until al dente. Reserve a cup of the cooking water before draining.
Dice the bacon and fry over medium heat for 5-7 minutes until crisp. Whisk the egg with the grated Parmesan and black pepper.
Take the bacon pan off the heat. Add the hot spaghetti and egg mixture and toss continuously, loosening with a little cooking water until creamy.
Serve with the washed rucola. For a fully cooked egg sauce, return to very low heat and stir continuously until it reaches 71 C; use pasteurized egg if keeping the sauce lightly cooked.

Cut the dipping vegetables into small pieces. Boil the potato for 10-15 minutes until tender; steam the broccoli, carrot, Brussels sprouts and baby corn until tender, adding each according to its size.

Bake the garlic bread and nuggets according to their packages; raw poultry nuggets must reach 74 C. Cook the mushroom in a non-stick pan with a splash of water until tender; serve the tomato and bell pepper raw.
Grate the Gruyère and Emmental. Combine the minced garlic and white wine in a small saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer.
Toss the grated cheeses with the cornstarch, then add to the wine a handful at a time, stirring over low heat until smooth. Add the nutmeg; loosen with a splash of water if needed.
Keep the fondue warm without boiling and serve with the measured assortment of bread, nuggets and vegetables. The listed dippers together form one portion, not separate full side dishes.
Cook the dry rice in water according to its package. Drain the kidney beans and chickpeas; dice the bell pepper, carrot and onion, and mince the garlic.
Heat the vegetable oil in a saucepan. Cook the onion, carrot and bell pepper for 5 minutes, then add the minced beef and cook for 5-7 minutes, breaking it up, until it reaches 71 C.
Stir in the garlic, cumin and tomato paste for 1 minute. Add the crushed tomato, beans and chickpeas with 100 ml water per two servings.
Season with the salt and black pepper and simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add a little water if the sauce becomes too thick.
Serve over the rice and finish with the chopped coriander. This is a mild, cumin-seasoned version.
Heat the oven grill. Melt the butter in a small saucepan, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the milk and simmer for 2-3 minutes until thick.
Season the bechamel with nutmeg, salt and black pepper. Spread the mustard on half the bread, add the ham and half the cheese, and close with the remaining bread.
Put the sandwich on a baking tray, cover with the bechamel and remaining cheese, and grill for 3-5 minutes until bubbling and golden; watch closely to prevent burning.
Heat the vegetable oil in a frying pan and fry the egg. Cook until both white and yolk are set, or use a pasteurized egg for a runny yolk. Put it on the sandwich and serve.
Peel and dice the potato, boil in water for 10-15 minutes until soft, then drain. Mash with the milk and cheese while hot.
Dice the onion and tomato. Mix with the olive oil, rice vinegar and salt to make the vinagrete; finely shred the cabbage.
Cook the peas in boiling water for 2-3 minutes. Heat the hot dog sausage according to its package until steaming throughout, and warm the bun.
Fill the bun with the sausage and potato puree. Add the ketchup, mayonnaise, vinagrete, cabbage and peas, then finish with Batata Palha and serve immediately.
Peel and cut the potatoes into evenly sized chunks. Boil in water for 15-20 minutes until tender, then drain.
Steam or boil the vegetable mix for 5-8 minutes, or according to its package, until tender.
Season the pork chops with the salt and black pepper. Heat the vegetable oil and fry for about 4-6 minutes per side, depending on thickness, until the centre reaches 63 C; rest for 3 minutes.
Divide the potatoes, vegetables and pork between plates. Spoon any pan juices over the meat.
Heat the oven to 220 C conventional or 200 C fan. Place the Lebanese wraps on baking trays.
Slice the mushroom and onion thinly. Spread the tomato sauce over the wraps, leaving a small border.
Top with the mozzarella, grated Gouda, ready-to-eat sliced meat, mushroom and onion, spreading everything evenly.
Bake for 8-12 minutes until the edges are crisp and the cheese is melted. Add the basil, slice and serve.
Heat the oven and bake the fish sticks according to their package, until piping hot and cooked through.
Peel and dice the potato. Boil in water for 12-15 minutes until tender, then drain and toss with half the butter.
Wilt the spinach in a saucepan with the remaining butter for 2-3 minutes; if using frozen spinach, cook according to its package. Season with the salt and black pepper.
Serve the fish sticks with the potatoes and spinach.
Poach the boneless fish in gently simmering water for 5-8 minutes, depending on thickness, until it reaches 63 C. Cool briefly, then flake and check for bones.
Cook the dry rice vermicelli according to its package, drain and rinse with cold water. Boil the bean sprouts for 2 minutes, then drain and cool.
Wash the lettuce and mint and cut the carrot into fine matchsticks. Mix the ready-to-use peanut sauce and hoisin sauce, adding a little water if needed for dipping.
Soften one rice-paper sheet at a time in warm water according to its package. Lay it flat and add a small share of fish, vermicelli, vegetables and mint.
Fold the sides inward and roll tightly. Repeat with the remaining sheets and serve with the dip. If not eating immediately, refrigerate promptly and eat the same day.
Mix the grated ginger, shoyu, rice vinegar, prepared chicken broth, sugar and sesame oil until the sugar dissolves. Chill the sauce.
Hard-boil the egg for 9-10 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and slice. Cut the cucumber, tomato, ready-to-eat roasted beef and surimi into strips.
Cook the dry noodles according to their package, drain and rinse thoroughly under cold water. Drain well so the sauce is not diluted.
Arrange the noodles and toppings in a bowl. Pour over the sauce and finish with sesame seeds, karashi mustard and beni shoga. Serve cold immediately or refrigerate promptly.
Cook the dry rice in water according to its package. Cut the meat into bite-sized pieces and dice the carrot, potato and onion.
Heat the vegetable oil in a saucepan. Brown the meat and onion for 4-5 minutes, then add the carrot and potato.

Add water in the amount recommended on the curry roux package for the listed roux quantity, generally about 150-200 ml per serving. Simmer for 15-20 minutes until the vegetables and meat are tender; chicken must reach 74 C if used.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the Japanese curry roux until dissolved. Return to low heat for 5 minutes, stirring until thickened, and serve with the rice.
Cook the dry rice in water according to its package. Thinly slice the onion and spring onion. Mix the prepared dashi, shoyu, mirin and sugar for the sauce.
Flatten the pork cutlet to about 1 cm thick and season with the salt and black pepper. Beat the Breadcrumb mix egg in one dish; put the flour and panko in separate dishes.

Coat the pork in flour, then egg, then panko. Discard any coating egg that touched raw pork. Heat the vegetable oil in a small frying pan and shallow-fry over medium heat for about 3-4 minutes per side until golden and at least 63 C inside; rest for 3 minutes.
Slice the cutlet. In a clean small pan, simmer the onion in the sauce for 4-5 minutes until soft, then lay the cutlet over it.
Beat the separate Final simmer egg and pour around the cutlet. Cover and simmer gently for 2-3 minutes until the egg is fully set and everything is hot throughout.
Slide the cutlet, onion, egg and sauce over the rice and finish with the spring onion.
Heat the oven to 190 C conventional or 170 C fan. Dice the onion and mince the garlic; heat the olive oil in a saucepan and soften the onion for 3 minutes.
Add the minced beef and cook until browned and at least 71 C. Add the garlic, tomato sauce, salt and black pepper and simmer for 5 minutes; wilt in the spinach.

Add about 100 ml water per serving to keep the sauce loose enough for the oven-ready sheets. In a small baking dish, alternate sauce, lasagna sheets and grated cheese, finishing with sauce and cheese.

Cover the dish and bake for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake for 10-15 minutes until the sheets are tender and the top is golden. Follow the sheet package if it requires longer cooking; rest for 5 minutes before serving.

Cook the dry rice according to its package, then spread on a clean tray until surface moisture evaporates and use immediately. If preparing ahead, refrigerate within 1 hour and use within 24 hours; do not leave rice at room temperature.
Dice the chicken, mince the garlic and slice the spring onion. Heat the vegetable oil in a wok and stir-fry the chicken for 5-7 minutes until it reaches 74 C.
Add the garlic and vegetable mix and stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until tender and hot throughout.
Add the rice and shoyu and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until steaming throughout. Finish with the spring onion and serve immediately; reheat refrigerated rice only once.
Mix the flour, prepared dashi, grated nagaimo, salt, Batter sugar, baking powder and egg. Fold in the finely shredded cabbage, sliced spring onion and tenkasu.
Mix the Sauce sugar, oyster sauce, ketchup and Worcestershire sauce until smooth. This is the measured homemade sauce; bottled okonomiyaki sauce may replace it, not be added alongside it.
Heat the vegetable oil in a non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Add the batter as one thick pancake per serving, then arrange the bacon on top.

Cover and cook for 5-6 minutes. Flip carefully, cover again and cook for another 5-6 minutes, until the bacon is cooked and the pancake centre reaches 71 C with no wet batter; lower the heat if it browns too quickly.
Turn onto a plate and spread with the homemade sauce. Finish with Japanese mayo, katsuobushi, shredded nori and beni shoga.
Cook the dry rice according to its package. Bake or fry the karaage chicken according to its package until hot throughout; raw chicken must reach 74 C.
Steam the broccoli for 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp. Grate the orange zest, reserving the flesh for serving, and mince the ginger and garlic.
Mix the orange juice, shoyu, rice vinegar, brown sugar, black pepper and zest. In a separate cup, mix the cornstarch with 20 ml cold water per two servings.

Heat the vegetable oil in a saucepan and cook the ginger and garlic for 30 seconds. Add the juice mixture, bring to a simmer, then stir in the cornstarch slurry and simmer for 1-2 minutes until glossy.
Toss the hot karaage in the sauce just before serving. Serve with rice, broccoli and the reserved orange flesh.
Heat the oven to 200 C conventional or 180 C fan. Dice the chicken, bell pepper, mushroom and onion.
Heat the vegetable oil in a frying pan and cook the chicken for 5-7 minutes until it reaches 74 C. Add the bell pepper, mushroom and onion and cook for another 4 minutes.
Stir half the salsa into the filling. Put the filling and half the cheddar on the tortilla, fold in the sides and roll tightly; place seam-side down on a baking tray.
Put the nachos alongside the burrito and scatter over the remaining cheddar. Bake for 8-10 minutes until the tortilla is crisp and the cheese has melted.
Serve with the diced tomato and avocado, sour cream and remaining salsa.
Cook the dry rice in water according to its package. Slice the onion, cut the boneless chicken thigh into bite-sized pieces, and slice the spring onion and parsley.
Combine the prepared dashi, shoyu, mirin and sugar in a wide pan. Add the onion and simmer for 4-5 minutes until softened.
Add the chicken and simmer gently for 6-8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until every piece is cooked and the centre reaches 74 C.
Lightly beat the eggs and pour evenly over the chicken. Cover and simmer over low heat for 2-3 minutes until the eggs are fully set.
Divide the rice between bowls and spoon the chicken, egg and sauce over it. Finish with the spring onion and parsley.
Whisk the flour, milk and egg into a smooth batter and rest for 10 minutes. Dice the bacon and chop any large pieces in the vegetable mix.
Fry the bacon in a non-stick pan until cooked, then add the vegetables and cook for 4-5 minutes until tender. Transfer to a plate.
Melt a little of the butter in the same pan over medium heat. Pour in enough batter for a thin pancake and scatter over a share of the bacon, vegetables and grated cheese.

Cook for 2-3 minutes until the surface starts to set, flip and cook for 1-2 minutes until no raw batter remains. Repeat with the remaining butter, batter and filling, making about two pancakes per serving.
Heat the oven to 200 C conventional or 180 C fan. Cook the dry rice in water according to its package. Flatten the chicken breast to about 1 cm thick.
Dice the onion and mince the garlic. Heat half the vegetable oil in a saucepan, soften the onion for 3 minutes, then add the garlic and tomato sauce and simmer for 5 minutes.

Beat the egg. Dip the chicken in the egg and then the panko, pressing to coat; discard any egg that touched raw chicken. Heat the remaining oil in a non-stick pan and brown the chicken for 2-3 minutes per side.
Put the chicken in a baking dish, cover with the tomato sauce and Parmesan, and bake for 12-15 minutes until the chicken centre reaches 74 C.
Wilt the spinach in a saucepan with a splash of water for 2-3 minutes. Serve the chicken with the rice and spinach.
Bring a saucepan of water to the boil. In a separate pan, heat the olive oil and cook the minced beef for 5-7 minutes, breaking it up, until it reaches 71 C.
Add the tomato sauce and simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the spinach and cook for 2-3 minutes until wilted.
Cook the chilled ravioli according to its package. Reserve a little cooking water, then drain gently.
Fold the ravioli into the meat sauce, loosening with cooking water if needed. Serve topped with the grated Parmesan.
Warm the prepared broth in a saucepan. Dice the chicken breast, zucchini and mushroom; finely chop the onion and garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan and cook the chicken for 5-7 minutes until it reaches 74 C. Add the zucchini and mushroom, cook for 3-4 minutes, then transfer to a plate.
Melt the butter in the pan and soften the onion for 3 minutes. Add the garlic and dry Arborio rice, stir for 1 minute, then pour in the white wine and let it mostly evaporate.

Add warm broth a ladle at a time, stirring frequently and waiting for each addition to be mostly absorbed. Cook for 18-22 minutes until the rice is tender with a slight bite; use hot water if the broth runs out.
Return the chicken and vegetables for the final 3 minutes, until hot throughout. Stir in the Parmesan, salt and black pepper, rest for 2 minutes, and top with the rucola.
Cook the dry rice in water according to its package. Slice the beef and mushroom, dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Heat the vegetable oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Sear the beef strips for 3-4 minutes until cooked through, then transfer to a plate.
Cook the onion and mushroom in the same pan for 5 minutes, adding a splash of water if needed. Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, mustard, salt and black pepper for 1 minute.
Add the cooking cream and 30 ml water per serving and simmer for 2 minutes. Return the beef and heat through, then take off the heat and stir in the sour cream without boiling.
Serve over the rice and scatter the Batata Palha over the top just before eating.
Dice the chicken and zucchini. Heat the vegetable oil in a pan and cook the chicken for 5-7 minutes until it reaches 74 C; add the zucchini and cook for 3-4 minutes until tender.
Mash the avocado and mix with the finely diced Guacamole tomato and onion. Wash the lettuce and slice the cucumber.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan. Spread with the cream cheese and hummus, then divide the chicken, zucchini, lettuce, cucumber and guacamole between them.
Add the salsa and grated cheese, fold in the sides and roll tightly. Serve immediately.
Mix the sesame oil, Worcestershire sauce, oyster sauce, ketchup, shoyu and sugar. Loosen the chilled yakisoba noodles according to their package.
Slice the pork, cabbage, carrot, onion and shiitake mushroom thinly, and cut the broccoli into small florets.

Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Stir-fry the pork for 4-5 minutes until cooked through, then add the vegetables and stir-fry for 4-5 minutes, using a splash of water to soften the broccoli.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss for 2-3 minutes until the noodles are steaming hot and evenly coated. Serve immediately.
Heat the oven to 180 C conventional or 160 C fan. Cook the dry rice in water according to its package. Dice the onion, apple and apricot, and mince the garlic.
Heat the vegetable oil in a frying pan and soften the onion for 4 minutes. Add the minced beef and cook until browned and at least 71 C, breaking it up.

Add the garlic, curry powder, cumin, cinnamon, salt, black pepper, apple and apricot and cook for 3 minutes. Stir in the cream cheese and transfer to a small baking dish; this is a simplified cream-cheese version.
Whisk the eggs, milk and turmeric and pour over the meat. Lay the bay leaves on top and bake for 25-30 minutes until the topping is fully set and the centre reaches 71 C.
Rest for 5 minutes and remove the bay leaves. Serve with the rice.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Wash and dry the lettuce, dice the tomato and cucumber, and put them in a bowl with the chickpeas.
Whisk the olive oil, juice from the listed lemon portion, mustard, salt and black pepper into a dressing.
Toss the salad with the dressing just before eating and serve with the bread. If packing ahead, refrigerate the salad and keep the dressing separate.
Place the eggs in boiling water and cook for 9-10 minutes until hard-boiled. Cool in cold water, peel and chop.
Mix the eggs with the mayonnaise, mustard, salt and black pepper. Wash and dry the lettuce.
Put the lettuce and egg filling between the bread slices. Serve immediately or refrigerate promptly until lunch.
Spread the mustard on the inside of the bread and fill with the ready-to-eat ham and grated or sliced cheese.
Spread the butter thinly on the outside. Cook in a frying pan over medium-low heat for 3-4 minutes per side, pressing gently, until golden and the cheese is melted.
Let the toastie stand for 1 minute, then cut and serve while warm.
Wash and dry the rucola and slice the tomato. Use ready-to-eat roasted beef, not raw beef.
Spread the mustard over the bread and layer with the roasted beef, tomato and rucola.
Close the sandwich and serve. Refrigerate promptly if packing it for later.
Heat the oven to 220 C conventional or 200 C fan. Slice the zucchini, bell pepper and onion and toss with the olive oil, salt and black pepper.
Spread the vegetables on a baking tray and roast for 15-20 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly browned.
Warm the dairy-free tortilla briefly in a dry pan. Spread with the hummus, add the roasted vegetables, fold in the sides and roll tightly.
Hard-boil the egg for 9-10 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and slice. Cut the cucumber and carrot into fine matchsticks.
Cook the dry noodles according to their package, drain and rinse under cold water. Drain thoroughly.
Whisk the shoyu, rice vinegar and sesame oil. Toss with the noodles, cucumber and carrot.
Top with the egg and sesame seeds. Serve cold immediately or refrigerate promptly until lunch.

Cook the dry rice according to its package, spread on a clean tray to let surface moisture evaporate and use immediately. For rice cooked ahead, refrigerate within 1 hour, use within 24 hours and reheat only once.
Beat the eggs and slice the spring onion. Heat half the vegetable oil in a wok and scramble the eggs until fully set, then transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, vegetable mix and peas and stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until tender and hot throughout.
Add the rice, shoyu and cooked eggs and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until steaming throughout. Finish with the spring onion and serve immediately.
Cook the dry spaghetti in water seasoned with half the salt until al dente. Reserve a cup of cooking water before draining.
Slice the chicken and mushroom, dice the onion and mince the garlic. Heat the olive oil and cook the chicken for 5-7 minutes until it reaches 74 C; transfer to a plate.
Cook the onion and mushroom in the same pan for 5 minutes, then add the garlic for 30 seconds. Stir in the cooking cream and a little pasta water and simmer for 2 minutes.
Return the chicken, add the spinach and cook until wilted and hot throughout. Season with the remaining salt and black pepper, then toss with the spaghetti, adding cooking water as needed.
Divide between plates and finish with the grated Parmesan.
